newsitem.title: ITALY: Castro plans Rome visit for World Food Summit.
newsitem.headline: Castro plans Rome visit for World Food Summit.

text.p: Cuban leader Fidel Castro intends to visit Rome next week to attend the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation's World Food Summit, FAO director-general Jacques Diouf said on Friday.
Diouf could not confirm that Castro was certain to make the trip but told reporters in response to questions: "We have information that Castro intends to come to attend the summit."
The summit, from November 13 to 17, will be the first conference among heads of state and government to tackle the challenge of how to feed the world.

Diouf, speaking after meeting Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, confirmed that FAO still expected some 100 heads of state and government to take part. The U.N. agency has not released names for what it says are security reasons.

Castro's presence could provide an opportunity for an historic meeting with Pope John Paul which could in turn lead to a visit by the Pontiff to the communist-ruled island, the only Spanish-speaking country in Latin America he has not visited.

Though Castro's engagements are routinely unannounced, diplomatic sources say a hotel has been booked for the Cuban leader in Rome for November 12 to 18 and meetings tentatively scheduled with Prodi and Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro.
